paper_metadata.title: Implementing Credit Risk Analysis with Quantum Singular Value Transformation

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum credit-risk workflow for VaR estimation using QSVT-based state preparation plus Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation on a 4-asset multivariate Gaussian conditional-independence model. The reported simulation study uses 2048 shots and a degree-1000 threshold polynomial, and benchmarks CDF estimates such as 0.5752 vs 0.5827 at loss 0 and 0.9990 vs 1.0018 at loss 89,654.78, with the final VaR converging to 54,807.94.

experiments.description: End-to-end gate-based quantum credit risk analysis for Value at Risk (VaR) estimation using QSVT-based state preparation and Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE), validated on a 4-asset multivariate Gaussian conditional independence model via simulation.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with QSVT-based state preparation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Counterparty default scenarios are encoded in an n-qubit counterparties register; losses are loaded into the amplitude of a target qubit via controlled y-rotations, then filtered with QSVT. The paper uses a multivariate Gaussian conditional independence model with 4 counterparties and 2 qubits per Gaussian risk factor.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the cumulative distribution function of aggregated losses to compute VaR at confidence level alpha_var; VaR_alpha(L) = inf{x in R | F_x(L) >= 1 - alpha_var}.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: QSVT polynomial approximation of a threshold function filters scenarios satisfying the target-loss condition; IQAE estimates the resulting amplitude. No penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Credit risk analysis on an anonymized and perturbed real dataset with 4 assets/counterparties and correlated risk factors.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Input values are taken from a suitably anonymized and perturbed database containing real, not synthetic, data. Gaussian factors are truncated at ±2.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation study; CDF values are benchmarked against classical reconstruction of scenario probabilities from the uncertainty operator U, and VaR is obtained via iterative bisection search. Number of shots: 2048.

hardware.classical_solver: QSPPACK (MATLAB) for polynomial coefficients/phases; iterative bisection search for VaR

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Polynomial approximation of the threshold function T_mu computed with QSPPACK; phase estimation for QSVT operators; classical benchmark CDF computed from simulated uncertainty operator U.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search over aggregated loss to recover VaR from estimated CDF; rescaling by k^2 is accounted for in post-processing.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: bisection search converges toward the target VaR

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speed-up is asymptotic; practical performance is limited by circuit cost and the QSVT approximation factor k^2.

speedup_claims.factor: O(d n) circuit depth for QSVT state preparation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: previous multi-risk-factor credit-risk circuits with exponential gate scaling in the number of counterparties
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that independence of d from n remains to be proved.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(d n) for the QSVT state-preparation circuit depth; IQAE complexity O(epsilon_IQAE^-1 log(alpha_IQAE^-1 log2(epsilon_IQAE^-1)))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo methods are the classical baseline; no explicit asymptotic complexity given in the paper for the benchmark implementation
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: The paper states the QAE/IQAE approach offers quadratic speed-up asymptotically, but the QSVT scaling introduces a constant multiplicative factor k^2 in amplitude estimation.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not established experimentally; paper reports a simulation study with IQAE and QSVT, degree d = 1000, 2048 shots, and a 4-asset credit-risk instance.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation is not enough to overcome constant-factor overheads in practice
State preparation and polynomial synthesis are classical preprocessing bottlenecks

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports a simulation study and does not name a real QPU.

num_qubits not explicitly stated; the paper describes registers C (n qubits), T (1 qubit), B (1 ancilla), and Z (auxiliary register for Gaussian factors), but does not give a total register count in a single number.
The paper presents a simulation study validating a QSVT-based state preparation for IQAE, but no experimental classical-vs-quantum advantage comparison is reported.
The instance is small and noiseless, so this is best classified as theoretical/noiseless-simulation evidence rather than demonstrated advantage.
